statement: The free stress tensor of a self-dual five-form in ten Lorentzian dimensions has vanishing trace at quadratic order, so Tr(tau) first contributes at field degree 4.

argument.step_1: the free stress tensor of a p-form is quadratic in F, so its trace is a degree-2 scalar
argument.step_2: every candidate trace is a multiple of the single quadratic Lorentz scalar <F,F>: for T_{mn} ~ F_{m...}F_n^{...} - c eta_{mn}<F,F> the trace is (1 - c d)<F,F> for ANY improvement coefficient c, so the conclusion is independent of the improvement term and of the overall normalisation
argument.step_3: F ^ F is a top form built from two copies of an ODD-degree form in even dimension, hence identically zero; <F,*F> is proportional to F ^ F, so it vanishes
argument.step_4: on either eigenspace of the star, F = +-*F gives <F,F> = +-<F,*F> = 0
argument.conclusion: the degree-2 part of Tr(tau) vanishes identically; the first possible contribution is degree 4

computational_verification.control_present: unprojected five-forms give NONZERO <F,F>, so the vanishing is not an artefact of the contraction routine

historical_note: the counterfactual reproduces exactly the earlier error in which the unconditional span gave rank 14 and quotient 0; it is retained as a negative regression fixture
remaining_for_mentor: confirmation that the free theory and stress-tensor convention used here are the intended ones, and that no formulation in use (PST, auxiliary-field, clone, Hamiltonian) changes the quadratic trace. The vanishing itself does not depend on the improvement coefficient, which narrows what confirmation is needed.
